integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] An original expressive 3D CG animated Brazilian street-news comedy at a peaceful protest by adult PC gamers. One uninterrupted static eye-level medium-wide portrait shot,768x1344,15seconds. Reporter screen-left, gamer screen-right, both fully original fictional adults, lively faces, visible hands and solid grounded bodies. A small asynchronous adult crowd stands behind them in a warm Brazilian square. Soft afternoon sunlight from screen-left, colorful matte clothes, coherent contact shadows. Plain red-brick storefront and plain navy awning. No existing character, real person, store name or numerical price claim. No violence, fire, weapons or damage.
Exactly TWO enormous plain pale ivory BLANK paper protest boards high above every head, fully front-facing, rectangular and nearly still. Left paper stays within x28to356, right within x412to740. Both boards lie above y480, with a generous air gap between the paper and all hair, hands, microphones and bodies. Both boards and all four corners stay fully visible for the entire shot. Separate supporters hold the wooden poles far below the papers. No occlusion and no board bouncing during laughter or chanting. Exactly two boards, no other signs. All paper surfaces have absolutely no letters, numbers, symbols, drawings or texture marks. Exact huge lettering will be composited later. Leave the upper navy awning plain without writing. All clothing, microphone and computer props are unbranded. No subtitles or other on-screen text.

Static eye-level medium-wide waist-up interview. Two huge blank boards occupy the upper third, above all hair. The entire small box and both actors hands remain visible. Reporter left, interviewee right, soft afternoon side light and the series brick facade/navy awning.

Reporter: original adult woman with short straight black pixie hair and mustard-yellow blazer, screen-left. Gamer: original adult man with dark curly hair and teal hoodie, screen-right. They are not recurring canonical characters.

A single small plain closed brown cardboard graphics-card box rests securely on a light wooden table. No text or logos. He indicates the box once with an open empty palm, then turns that palm upward in disbelief. He never lifts the box, transfers objects or opens it.

The gamer tries to justify abandoning a supposedly great deal. He starts sincerely pleased on the promotion, briefly pauses, then becomes incredulous on the shipping charge and lands the entire-truck punchline as a dry accusation at the imaginary quote. The reporter keeps a professional face until his last word, looks down at the tiny box, looks back at him, tries to suppress a laugh and fails.

ACTING SCORE: Play the ridiculous answer as a sincere attempt to convince the reporter. Start with engaged curiosity and attentive listening, not constant grinning. One dominant meaningful gesture accompanies the answer. The reporter perceives the punchline only after its final word, glances briefly toward the relevant prop, then tries to suppress a smile and fails. The laugh is clearly visible and AUDIBLE: microphone lowers to waist, eyes squeeze, head tips back briefly, then a small forward lean with two uneven shoulder bounces and one hand against the abdomen. The gamer holds a straight face for a short recognition beat, then cracks into an amused grin and joins with a shorter irregular voiced laugh. Nearby supporters react later and differently; no synchronized mechanical swaying. Both catch their breath and exchange an amused look. Laughter must have a cause in this exchange. Keep feet planted, prop supported and boards motionless. No frozen faces, talking-mouth-only acting, anticipation before the joke, flat monotone or tiny polite chuckle.

Exactly TWO verbal turns in native Brazilian Portuguese. Reporter(S1), an adult female voice, asks once at 0.2 to 2.4 seconds, curious and attentive: <d>[Portuguese] Por que você desistiu da placa?</d> Reporter then listens with closed lips. Gamer(S2), an adult male voice, answers once at 2.8 to 9.7 seconds, with clear ordinary conversational Brazilian Portuguese diction, mock seriousness and a brief pause between sentences: <d>[Portuguese] A placa entrou em promoção. Mas, pelo frete, acho que estão me vendendo o caminhão inteiro!</d> No repeated words or additional utterances. Reporter reacts only after the last word, with a short recognition beat, an unsuccessful attempt to hold a smile, microphone lowered below the mouth, then a clear AUDIBLE warm voiced belly laugh. Eyes close, shoulders bounce twice unevenly, body leans forward briefly and recovers. Gamer joins later with a shorter clearly audible spontaneous laugh. The crowd reacts after the two leads, with different timing, never synchronized swaying. Laughing is nonverbal: no invented words, babble or extra syllables. Let the uneven voiced laughing reaction play from 10.1 to 13.8 seconds, followed by a natural breath and recovery through 15 seconds. No words during laughter or recovery.

One static continuous shot, normal speed, no cuts or zoom. Only specified exact dialogue tags contain spoken words. Laughter is native in-scene nonverbal voiced laughter with irregular breaths, not extra syllables or words. No canned laugh track, narrator, music, subtitles, logos, watermarks or added verbal remarks. Keep background street ambience soft under dialogue and laughter.
overall_soundscape: Expressive clearly intelligible on-screen native Brazilian Portuguese voices and spontaneous warm voiced laughter synchronized with bodily reactions, with low outdoor ambience.
